notes.meaning: David calls out to God in his distress, asking Him to listen and show mercy. He remembers that when he was hemmed in and squeezed by trouble in the past, God made room for him to escape. Because God has always been faithful before, David boldly asks for grace once again. Remembering how God helped us in our past troubles gives us confidence to pray today.

differ.view: God is called the God of righteousness because He makes believers right with Himself by giving them the righteousness of His Son.
God is called the God of righteousness because He knows David is innocent of the charges against him and acts as the defender of his just cause.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Early church writers like Augustine read the opening words as a statement of praise that God had already heard the prayer and brought the soul out of narrow sorrow into the open space of joy.

notes.meaning: David turns to challenge powerful men who are attacking his reputation and trying to ruin his royal standing. He asks how long they will chase after empty schemes and spread harmful lies to hurt him. Their plans against God's appointed leader are completely useless and bound to fail.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine explained this as a warning against seeking happiness in passing earthly things, since only God's unchanging truth makes a person truly blessed.

notes.meaning: David tells his enemies that the Lord has chosen the godly person and set him apart for Himself. God claims His servant as His own special treasure and guards him closely. Because of this personal bond, David knows the Lord will definitely answer when he calls.

differ.view: This passage highlights God's sovereign election, pointing out that God chooses and separates His people entirely by His own gracious choice.
This verse shows that God chooses and specially protects the person who responds to Him by living a life of sincere love, reverence, and obedience.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine applied the phrase 'set apart' directly to Jesus Christ, whom God raised from the dead and exalted to His right hand in heaven.

notes.meaning: David warns his hearers to tremble before God and stop sinning against Him. When they go to bed at night, they should examine their own hearts quietly instead of plotting trouble or acting in anger. Taking time to be silent before the Lord helps calm our thoughts and keeps us from wrongdoing.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine taught that this means either controlling our first stirs of anger before they become action, or feeling a righteous anger toward our own past sins so we turn away from them.

notes.meaning: David commands the people to bring proper sacrifices with clean hands and upright hearts, rather than leaning on empty ceremonies. Going through the motions of religion means nothing to God if our hearts are far from Him. True worship must always be paired with sincere, humble trust in the Lord.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Augustine interpreted these sacrifices as the offering of a broken and sorrowful heart, which produces the good deeds of a transformed life.

notes.meaning: Many discouraged people wander around looking for someone to show them any kind of earthly relief or prosperity. David ignores these complaints and asks the Lord to shine the light of His face upon them instead. God's loving favor and presence bring far greater peace than anything this world can provide.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Catholic teaching connects the light of God's face stamped upon us to the light of moral reason in the human soul, by which people recognize what is good and true.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Scholars explain that shining the light of one's face is a traditional Hebrew picture for an approving smile that conveys divine goodwill and blessing.

notes.meaning: The Lord has given David a deep, inward happiness that earthly wealth can never equal. Farmers celebrated with tremendous excitement when their crops of grain and fresh wine were plentiful at harvest time. Yet the quiet joy of having God's presence in the heart is far sweeter and lasts much longer.

David can lie down and fall asleep immediately because his heart is completely at rest. Even though danger and enemies may surround him, he knows that God alone keeps him safe through the night. True peace comes from resting securely in God's unending protection.

other.label: Modern scholarship
other.view: Some scholars note that the word 'alone' can refer to David dwelling in solitary safety, cut off and protected from outside danger by the Lord.
